title: Pangram 4 targets mixed human-and-AI writing, with a higher API price
friendlyTitle: Pangram updates its tool for finding AI-written text
summary: Pangram has launched a larger text detector designed to identify AI-assisted passages, mixed authorship and output processed by humaniser tools. The company reports a 0.0041% false-positive rate on internal tests, while changing API billing to $0.05 per 100 words and retiring Pangram 3 in September.
friendlySummary: Pangram 4 tries to find text written partly or fully by AI, including text changed by tools that make it sound human. The company also changed its prices.
whyItMatters: Publishers, schools and compliance teams gain more granular signals, but detection remains probabilistic and the headline numbers are vendor-reported. Decisions affecting people should use evidence and review rather than treating one detector score as proof.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The tool may help people review content, but its score is not proof. A person should check the evidence before making an important decision.
